reason: A keeps the original's centered stack with an even vertical rhythm. Logo, can, headline and CTA are well spaced, legal text is anchored at the bottom, and the can grew with the format. Its flaws: the decorative circles were shrunk into fully visible floating discs that no longer bleed off the edges, and the bottom-left disc looks arbitrary beside the CTA. B lets the big teal circle sit behind the logo and the can, which muddies the logo's clear space. The whole stack is pushed down, leaving dead space at the top, the can is smaller, and the legal line floats mid-canvas on the bottom-left circle above a large empty band at the bottom.

A reads cleanly left to right: bottle, then the centred wordmark, headline and subcopy, then the CTA. Its flaws: the bottle is jammed against the left and top edges, the decorative circles shrink to arbitrary dots (the peach one crowds the bottle's base, the green one floats above the CTA), and the subcopy runs long and small. B is cramped and collides: the oversized 'fizz' runs into the stacked circles at top right, the headline sits tight against the top edge, the bottle and CTA crowd the bottom and right edges, the subcopy wraps awkwardly over three lines, and SOLSTICE is pushed to a vertically centred spot at the far left, cut off from the headline.

A drops the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow, sets the body copy almost as large as the headline, and shrinks the 'Reserve a Case' CTA into a tiny pill in the right column. That CTA ends up the same size as the illegible legal block, which wrecks the hierarchy and leaves the two columns lopsided. B keeps the original's centred reading order (eyebrow, headline, body, prominent CTA, ship note, legal) with the brand intact, but it is cramped: the headline packs tightly under the eyebrow, there is little breathing room between blocks, and the legal text is oversized compared with the 'Ships late June' line.

A: the headline runs almost to the right edge with no margin, and it starts at a different left edge (~64px) from the brand mark and subhead (~76px). The 'Shop Flavours' CTA floats mid-right, cut off from the copy column, and the flavour pills are pushed to the bottom with a dead gap above them. The peach circle has shrunk to a stray dot in the corner. B: one clean left-aligned column (brand, a two-line headline, subhead, pills, CTA) with a clear hierarchy. Its flaws: the peach shape looks slightly squashed into an oval, and the right half is fairly empty apart from that shape.

A: clear center headline with the CTA at the right reads left to right, but the date block on the left is crowded against the logo, the subtitle wraps to an orphan line ("of the year"), the RSVP sits apart from its URL in the center, and the missing-asset placeholder collides with the bottom-right corner. B: the CTA has shrunk to a pill no bigger than the tag pills, so it is buried among them. The headline is cramped into the lower left, the subtitle is squeezed into a narrow column, and the date heading sits far above its own detail line. The small text (URL, legal) is scattered in tiny fragments, the logo is clipped by the planet edge, and the placeholder is crammed in.

A: the plan cards are shrunk to tiny tiles whose MONTHLY/YEARLY/FAMILY labels and 'per month' text can't be read, and the order is shuffled to 6/80/48. The legal copy is stacked in a cramped right column at nearly the same size as the subhead, and the headline is the only thing that reads. B: keeps the three cards in their original order, readable and on brand, with the dark Yearly card highlighted. However, the headline is smaller than the prices and wraps awkwardly ('fits / your week'), the CTA is pushed against the right edge, and the one-line legal footer is tiny and sits tight to the cards.

A: the oversized teal circle now sits behind the GLACIER logo and the right half of the can, so the brand mark and product collide with the decoration. The legal line floats mid-canvas, overlapping the light-blue circle and leaving dead space below it, and there is a large empty gap above the logo. B: keeps the original structure. The logo is clear of the circle, the can stays prominent, headline and CTA are centred in order, and the legal line sits at the bottom margin. Only minor polish is needed: the top-right circle crowds the can's right dot a little, and the CTA is slightly narrow relative to the headline.

A is cramped: the 'fizz' of the headline runs into the decorative circles, which are crushed together and clipped in the top-right corner. The CTA sits jammed close to the right edge, and the body copy wraps into a tight 3-line block squeezed between the bottle and the button. B is a clean left-to-right banner (bottle, centered brand/headline/one-line copy, CTA) with real breathing room, but it has flaws: the headline is undersized for the banner, the body copy and CTA label are small, the green circle floats awkwardly right above the CTA, the tiny yellow circle looks like debris, and the bottle cap nearly touches the top edge.

A keeps the original order and hierarchy (eyebrow, headline, body, orange CTA, ships note, legal), but it is cramped: the header band is squeezed, the gaps between headline, body and CTA are tight, the body copy is almost as heavy as the headline, and the legal text is too small to read. B drops the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow and shrinks the CTA to a tiny, unreadable pill in the right column. That buries the CTA under oversized body copy on the left. The legal text and 'Ships late June' are also crammed next to the button, so B's hierarchy and grouping are broken.

A: tidy left-aligned stack (brand, wrapped headline, subhead, chips, CTA) on one shared edge, with clear hierarchy and the decorative circles kept in the corners. Its flaws are minor: the right half is fairly empty and the CTA sits a little close to the bottom edge. B: the headline runs almost to the right edge with no margin, and the subhead is indented off the headline's left edge. The CTA floats on the right, cut off from the copy, and the flavour chips have been pushed below it into a detached row, so the reading order is jumbled and there is a large dead gap in the middle.

A is a jumbled patchwork: the headline is split across two big lines that fight the tall italic subtitle column; the RSVP button is shrunk to pill size and lumped in with the FREE ENTRY/ALL AGES/TASTINGS tags, so the CTA gets lost; the date block, URL and legal text float as separate pieces; and the SOLSTICE logo text is clipped by a dot ('SOLST CE'). B has a sensible three-column banner, a clear centred headline, grouped tags and a prominent RSVP button on the right, but the subtitle leaves an orphaned 'of the year' line, the left date block crowds the edge, and the missing-asset placeholder box is visible next to the CTA.

A keeps the three plan cards readable and in their original Monthly/Yearly/Family order, and reads left to right through to the CTA. But it is badly cramped: the cards nearly touch the top edge, the legal line is jammed along the bottom, the price numerals compete with a fairly small headline, and the subhead wraps awkwardly. B gives the headline strong hierarchy, but it shrinks the plan cards into tiny chips whose labels and 'per month' text can't be read. It also reorders them to 6/80/48, which breaks the sequence. The 48 card butts against the CTA, and the subhead and legal copy are crammed into a ragged block against the right edge, so the core pricing message is lost.

A keeps headline and CTA grouped as in the original, but the headline wraps to leave 'fizz' orphaned on its own line, and the CTA sits tight under it with the content crowded into the top 80%. B keeps the headline on one line and enlarges the bag, but the CTA drifts about 100px below the headline, so the two no longer read as a group; the CTA also shrinks and almost touches the olive circle at the bottom-left corner.

A reads cleanly left to right (logo, can, headline, sale ribbon, CTA), but the can is shrunk to a tiny icon, the legal line sits right under the headline at near-illegible size, and the red ribbon is wedged tight against the CTA. B has a strong headline, but the logo is tiny and crowded by a decorative circle, the tilted sale ribbon is jammed into the bottom-left corner and nearly clipped, and the legal text wraps to three cramped lines under the CTA, running into the bottom edge, so the right side is overstuffed.

A keeps the headline on one line and the bag large, but the small 'Find a Store' pill sits about 100px below the headline, cut off from its copy, and its left edge touches the olive circle in the bottom-left corner. B wraps the headline so 'fizz' is left alone on its own line and leaves some dead space at the bottom, but the headline, CTA and bag form one tight, centred group, and the larger CTA stands out more.

A: the logo is jammed against a decorative circle, the tilted sale banner runs down into the bottom-left edge and sits on a circle, the can is tiny, and the legal copy is a large, ragged 4-line block under the CTA that competes with it. B: reads cleanly left to right (logo, can, headline, sale banner, CTA) with the legal line small and subordinate under the headline. Its flaws are a thumbnail-sized can, a sale banner wedged tightly between the headline and CTA, and a little stray bubble decoration under the CTA.

A keeps the original's centred stack and calm feel, but the gap between the headline and the subcopy (~110px) is much larger than the gap from subcopy to CTA, so the block reads as two pieces. The subcopy also leaves 'flavours.' alone on its own line, and the headline is a bit small for the square. B's oversized 4-line headline dominates well, but the subcopy and CTA are squeezed side by side into a cramped bottom strip close to the bottom edge. Its centred 3-line subcopy doesn't line up with the button or the headline's edges, and the row breaks the original's single-column reading order.

A keeps the original reading order (eyebrow, headline, body, product, CTA), and the peach circle now sits behind the bottle as a clear backdrop. Its flaws are small: the body copy leaves 'sparkling.' alone on the second line, the text column is left-aligned while the bottle and CTA are centred, and there is a slightly large gap above the button. B moves 'WEEKEND ONLY' below the body copy, which breaks the eyebrow-headline order. The circle is cropped awkwardly behind the headline, the top band is empty, the bottle and CTA are cramped together while the bottom is left empty, and the body copy has the same orphan 'sparkling.'

A keeps the original's left-to-right banner logic with a large phone, a centred headline and subcopy block, and a stacked badge and button. However, the 'Try It' button is jammed about 10px from the right edge, the badge is tiny and floats high, and there is dead space above and below the text column. B sets the headline high with no breathing room and inflates the button and the 'Online Only' badge so the CTA competes with the headline. The badge and button are crammed into the bottom-right corner while the area under the subcopy sits empty, and the phone is shrunk, so the layout feels top-heavy and less like the original.

A breaks the original grouping. The headline sits alone on the left. 'Out now.' has moved off the headline and dangles to the right of the CTA as an orphan. The Try It button is jammed against the bottom of the product circle, so the right side is a cramped stack while the middle is dead space, and the reading order is muddled. B keeps the original order (product, then headline, subline and CTA), and the text column shares a clean left edge with good hierarchy. Its only flaws are minor: the large circle nearly touches the top and bottom edges, and the right margin is a bit empty.

A fills the 4:5 canvas sensibly: the headline, details block and RSVP keep strong sizes, and the pills stay readable. But the large cropped sun circle has shrunk to a small disc in the top-left corner, which changes the original's feel. There is also a large empty gap between the pills and the CTA, and the left-aligned details block still sits off the centred axis. B is just the original shrunk to about 80%: the pill labels and the URL line are tiny, and the content sits high, leaving roughly 130px of dead space at the bottom. The missing-asset placeholder floats arbitrarily at the right, so B reads as a scaled copy rather than a re-layout.

A fills the square well with a strong 4-line headline, but the bottom row is weak: the subhead becomes a centred 3-line block ('Now in / four flavours.') beside the CTA, and neither lines up with the headline's edges, so it feels improvised and cramped against the large headline. B keeps the original's single centred column, but the headline is undersized for the square. It also leaves a big, uneven gap between headline and subhead compared with the gap between subhead and CTA, the subhead wraps to an orphaned 'flavours.', and there is dead orange space top and bottom, so it reads as the banner shrunk onto a larger canvas.

A breaks the reading order: the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow now sits below the body copy instead of above the headline. It also leaves a dead band at the top and runs the '20% off' headline over the peach circle, which no longer reads as a backdrop for the bottle. B keeps the original order (eyebrow, headline, copy, product, CTA), puts the circle back behind the bottle as in the original, and keeps a clean left edge. Its flaws are minor: 'sparkling.' wraps onto a line of its own, and the gap between the bottle and the CTA is slightly too large.

A has a clear two-tier structure, with the headline and subcopy on top and the CTA and badge on a lower row, but the oversized 'Try It' pill crowds the bottom-right corner, the tilted badge nearly collides with it, and the bottom-left under the copy is dead space. B lets the phone and cropped circle dominate the left third, leaves a large empty band above the headline, and squeezes the badge and a small CTA into a column jammed against the right edge with the badge near the top edge, so the CTA is weakened and the right side looks cramped.

A keeps the original order (product circle, then headline, subline and CTA stacked on one left edge) with clear hierarchy. The circle crowds the left and bottom edges, and the right third is a little empty. B breaks the structure: the headline floats alone on the left, the circle is jammed against the top, and the CTA touches the circle. 'Out now.' sits as an orphan beside the button, so the reading order is jumbled and grouping is lost.

A looks like a shrunk copy. The headline, chips (tiny 'FREE ENTRY/ALL AGES' text) and CTA are all scaled down and float in the middle, leaving a dead band at the bottom (~120 px below the off-centre partner placeholder). Its sun circle is oversized and crowds the logo. B fills the width better: the headline, date block and chips are larger and more readable, the CTA is bigger and the partner box is centred. But its left-aligned date block (x≈50) does not line up with the centred headline axis or the can graphic, and the bottom 15% is still empty, so it needs polish.

A: the SOLSTICE wordmark sits off to the left of the headline instead of above it, and the 'Back by Demand' badge is the same size and weight as the CTA, so the CTA gets lost in a cramped 2x2 block. The phone is jammed against the top and bottom edges, there's a big empty gap between the phone and the text, and the right fifth of the banner is dead space. B: reads left to right like a proper banner (brand, one-line headline, subline, then badges, then CTA), and the hierarchy is clear. Still has flaws: the badges float in the middle, away from the copy, and their small text is hard to read; the gaps between groups are uneven, and the CTA sits tight to the right edge.

A: the lilac circle has come off the product and now sits behind the top-right copy, so 'WEEKEND ONLY' and '20% off' run over its edge. The headline is crammed almost to the right edge, the CTA pill stretches nearly the full canvas width, and the product floats alone in a dead middle zone with no backdrop. B: the circle stays behind the product as in the original. Copy, CTA and fine print share one clean left edge, and the order runs headline, product, then CTA. Its flaws are minor: the CTA is a bit far below the circle, there is some empty space at the bottom, and the fine print is small.

A: the bottle-in-circle hero is well placed and the headline is strong. But the NEW and Try It row is centred while the headline is left-aligned (they share no edge), a stray faint circle floats in the top-left corner, and the bottom band is a little empty. B: the bottle sticks out of its circle and is jammed against the top edge in a cramped corner. The NEW badge is enlarged to the size of a button and competes with the CTA. Both buttons are oversized and right-aligned, out of step with the left-aligned headline, which makes the layout lopsided and clumsy.

A works as a clean left-to-right leaderboard: the phone sits in its circle, the brand, one-line headline and subhead are stacked, the badges are stacked in the middle and the CTA sits on the right. Its flaws are small: the phone is very small, the circle is cropped at the top and bottom, and the badges sit apart from the copy. B has a large empty gap between the phone and the text. SOLSTICE floats off to the left of the headline, the two-line headline is cramped against the top edge, and the subhead is tiny. Its CTA is jammed under the 'Back by demand' badge in a crowded 2x2 cluster, and the CTA is no wider than that badge, so the call to action loses its prominence and the right side ends with an empty gap.

A is a clean top-to-bottom reflow: the left-aligned text block, the product centred on the lilac circle and the CTA below it read in the right order. Its flaws are minor: the product is small inside a large circle, there are uneven gaps around the CTA, and the legal line is tiny. B makes "20% off" so large it nearly touches the right edge. It cuts the circle off at the top corner so it sits behind the headline instead of the product, and leaves the product floating alone at the bottom. The CTA is jammed against the subhead, and the fine print is about as large as the subhead, which weakens the hierarchy.

A: the bottle is cropped at the top canvas edge and sticks out of its small circle, which is jammed into the top-left corner. The NEW pill is blown up nearly as big as the CTA, and the pills are pushed to the right edge while the headline is left-aligned, leaving a large dead area at lower left. B: the bottle is a well-proportioned centred hero and the hierarchy is clear, but the headline is left-aligned while the circle and the NEW/Try It row are centred, so it mixes two axes. The pill row also looks a little small and floats with uneven space below.
